about: How databases work, in our own words, the same for every database: 5 layers -> causes -> the complaints they explain. Each database's own error codes, words and exact commands live in app/dbknow/dialects/. Learned from official documentation first, then real users' problems.

parser.en: Command layer (the database couldn't read the command)
parser.hi: Command layer (database command padh nahi paya)

schema.en: Rules layer (the data broke a rule of the table)
schema.hi: Rules layer (data ne table ka koi rule toda)

resources.en: Capacity layer (the server ran out of something)
resources.hi: Capacity layer (server mein kuch khatam ho gaya)

transactions.en: Many-users layer (two jobs got in each other's way)
transactions.hi: Many-users layer (do kaam ek doosre ke raste mein aaye)

gateway.en: Door layer (the app couldn't get in)
gateway.hi: Door layer (app andar nahi aa payi)

syntax_error.title_en: The command has a grammar mistake near "{token}"
syntax_error.title_hi: Command mein "{token}" ke paas grammar ki galti hai
syntax_error.why_en: Before running anything, the database reads the command word by word. At "{token}" it found something that doesn't fit the grammar (often a missing comma, an unclosed quote or bracket, or a word that belongs to another database's dialect), so it refused to run any of it.
syntax_error.why_hi: Chalane se pehle database command ko shabd-shabd padhta hai. "{token}" pe use kuch aisa mila jo grammar mein fit nahi hota (aksar comma missing, quote/bracket band nahi, ya doosre database ka syntax), isliye usne kuch bhi nahi chalaya.
syntax_error.confirm_en: Run the corrected command; it is accepted without the error.
syntax_error.confirm_hi: Sahi command chalao; error nahi aayega.
syntax_error.prevent_en: Build queries with parameters (never by joining strings), and lint SQL in your code review or CI before it reaches production.
syntax_error.prevent_hi: Queries parameters se banao (string jodkar nahi), aur production se pehle SQL ko lint/check karo.

reserved_word.title_en: "{token}" is a reserved word of the database
reserved_word.why_en: Words like ORDER, GROUP, KEY, DESC, USER are part of the command language. Used as a table or column name without quoting, the database reads them as a command word and the grammar breaks there.
reserved_word.why_hi: ORDER, GROUP, KEY, DESC, USER jaise shabd command language ke hain. Bina quote ke table/column naam ki tarah likhne par database inhe command samajhta hai aur grammar wahin toot jaati hai.
reserved_word.confirm_en: The command runs once the name is quoted.
reserved_word.confirm_hi: Naam quote karte hi command chal jayegi.
reserved_word.prevent_en: Avoid reserved words as names (order -> orders, key -> item_key); quote identifiers in generated SQL.
reserved_word.prevent_hi: Reserved shabd naam mein mat rakho (order -> orders, key -> item_key); generated SQL mein naam quote karo.
reserved_word.short_en: A reserved word used as a name
reserved_word.short_hi: Reserved shabd naam ki tarah use hua

unknown_table.why_en: The command names a table the database can't find in this database: a typo, a different letter case, the wrong database selected, or a table that was never created (a migration that didn't run).
unknown_table.why_hi: Command mein aisi table ka naam hai jo is database mein nahi mili: spelling, capital/small letters, galat database chuna hua, ya table bani hi nahi (migration nahi chali).
unknown_table.confirm_en: List the tables and check the exact name; the command runs with the right one.
unknown_table.confirm_hi: Tables ki list dekho aur sahi naam lo; sahi naam se command chalegi.
unknown_table.prevent_en: Run migrations in deploy before the new code goes live; keep table names lower-case with underscores.
unknown_table.prevent_hi: Deploy mein naya code chalne se pehle migrations chalao; table naam small letters aur underscore mein rakho.
unknown_table.short_hi: Aisi table jo hai hi nahi

unknown_column.title_en: Column "{column}" doesn't exist in that table
unknown_column.title_hi: Column "{column}" us table mein nahi hai
unknown_column.why_en: The command uses a column name the table doesn't have: a typo, an old name after a rename, a column from another table used without joining it, or (PostgreSQL) a text value written in double quotes, which PostgreSQL reads as a column name.
unknown_column.why_hi: Command aisa column use karti hai jo table mein nahi: spelling, rename ke baad purana naam, doosri table ka column bina join ke, ya (PostgreSQL) text value double quotes mein, jise PostgreSQL column naam samajhta hai.
unknown_column.confirm_en: Check the table's columns; the command runs with the real name.
unknown_column.confirm_hi: Table ke columns dekho; asli naam se command chalegi.
unknown_column.prevent_en: Keep schema and code changes in the same release; in PostgreSQL use single quotes for text and double quotes only for names.
unknown_column.prevent_hi: Schema aur code ka badlav ek saath release karo; PostgreSQL mein text ke liye single quote, naam ke liye hi double quote.
unknown_column.short_hi: Aisa column jo hai hi nahi

ambiguous_column.title_en: Column "{column}" exists in more than one joined table
ambiguous_column.title_hi: Column "{column}" join ki gayi ek se zyada tables mein hai
ambiguous_column.why_en: When two joined tables both have a column with the same name (often id, name, created_at), the database can't know which one you mean unless the table is written in front of it.
ambiguous_column.why_hi: Jab join ki do tables mein same naam ka column ho (aksar id, name, created_at), to database nahi jaanta kaunsa chahiye jab tak aage table ka naam na likho.
ambiguous_column.confirm_en: Prefix the column with its table (users.{column}); the command runs.
ambiguous_column.confirm_hi: Column ke aage table ka naam lagao (users.{column}); command chalegi.
ambiguous_column.prevent_en: Always write table.column (or alias.column) in queries that join tables.
ambiguous_column.prevent_hi: Join wali queries mein hamesha table.column (ya alias.column) likho.
ambiguous_column.short_en: A column name found in two joined tables
ambiguous_column.short_hi: Do joined tables mein same column naam

unknown_function.title_en: Function "{token}" doesn't exist in this database
unknown_function.title_hi: Function "{token}" is database mein nahi hai
unknown_function.why_en: Each database has its own functions. A function from another database (IFNULL vs COALESCE, NOW() vs CURRENT_TIMESTAMP, GROUP_CONCAT vs STRING_AGG) or wrong argument types make it unknown here.
unknown_function.why_hi: Har database ke apne functions hote hain. Doosre database ka function (IFNULL vs COALESCE, GROUP_CONCAT vs STRING_AGG) ya galat type ke arguments se wo yahan unknown ho jata hai.
unknown_function.confirm_en: The command runs with this database's function.
unknown_function.confirm_hi: Is database ke function se command chalegi.
unknown_function.prevent_en: Prefer standard SQL functions (COALESCE, CAST, CURRENT_TIMESTAMP) in code meant for more than one database.
unknown_function.prevent_hi: Ek se zyada database wale code mein standard functions (COALESCE, CAST, CURRENT_TIMESTAMP) use karo.
unknown_function.short_en: A function this database doesn't have
unknown_function.short_hi: Aisa function jo is database mein nahi

group_by_strict.title_en: A selected column isn't in GROUP BY
group_by_strict.title_hi: Select kiya column GROUP BY mein nahi hai
group_by_strict.why_en: With GROUP BY, every selected column must either be grouped or summarised (SUM, MAX, COUNT...). Otherwise the database would have to pick a random row's value, and strict mode refuses that.
group_by_strict.why_hi: GROUP BY ke saath har select kiya column ya to group mein ho ya summary (SUM, MAX, COUNT...) mein. Warna database ko kisi bhi random row ki value leni padti, strict mode ye mana karta hai.
group_by_strict.confirm_en: The query runs and every row of the result is well defined.
group_by_strict.confirm_hi: Query chalegi aur result ki har value saaf hogi.
group_by_strict.prevent_en: Keep strict mode on (it prevents silently wrong reports) and write explicit aggregates.
group_by_strict.prevent_hi: Strict mode on rakho (ye chupchaap galat report rokta hai) aur saaf aggregate likho.
group_by_strict.short_en: A selected column missing from GROUP BY

duplicate_key.title_en: The value "{value}" already exists in a unique field ({key})
duplicate_key.title_hi: Value "{value}" pehle se ek unique field ({key}) mein hai
duplicate_key.why_en: A UNIQUE rule (or the primary key) allows each value only once. The row being saved carries "{value}", which another row already has, so the database refuses the whole statement to keep the rule true. Common real causes: a form submitted twice, a retry after a timeout, importing the same file again, or an auto-increment counter behind the data after an import.
duplicate_key.why_hi: UNIQUE rule (ya primary key) har value sirf ek baar allow karta hai. Save ho rahi row mein "{value}" hai, jo kisi aur row mein pehle se hai, isliye database poora statement mana kar deta hai. Asli wajah aksar: form do baar submit, timeout ke baad retry, same file dobara import, ya import ke baad auto-increment counter peeche reh gaya.
duplicate_key.confirm_en: Look up the existing row with that value; after the fix, saving no longer fails.
duplicate_key.confirm_hi: Us value wali maujood row dekho; fix ke baad save fail nahi hoga.
duplicate_key.prevent_en: Use an upsert (insert-or-update) where the same record can arrive twice, make the save idempotent (a request key), and keep sequences/auto-increment ahead of imported data.
duplicate_key.prevent_hi: Jahan same record do baar aa sakta hai wahan upsert (insert ya update) use karo, save ko idempotent banao (request key), aur import ke baad sequence/auto-increment aage rakho.
duplicate_key.short_en: A value that must be unique already exists

fk_missing_parent.title_en: The linked record ("{value}" in {parent}) doesn't exist
fk_missing_parent.title_hi: Jude hue record ("{parent}" mein "{value}") maujood nahi
fk_missing_parent.why_en: A foreign key says every child row must point to a real parent row. The row being saved points to a {parent} entry that isn't there, so saving it would leave an orphan, and the database refuses.
fk_missing_parent.why_hi: Foreign key kehti hai har child row ek asli parent row ko point kare. Save ho rahi row {parent} ki aisi entry ko point karti hai jo hai hi nahi, isliye database mana karta hai (warna anaath row ban jaati).
fk_missing_parent.confirm_en: Create the parent first (or use the right id); the save then goes through.
fk_missing_parent.confirm_hi: Pehle parent banao (ya sahi id lo); phir save ho jayega.
fk_missing_parent.prevent_en: Save parent and child in one transaction, parent first; validate ids in the app before saving.
fk_missing_parent.prevent_hi: Parent aur child ek transaction mein save karo, pehle parent; save se pehle app mein id check karo.

fk_has_children.title_en: Other rows still point to this record
fk_has_children.title_hi: Doosri rows abhi bhi is record ko point karti hain
fk_has_children.why_en: The record being deleted (or whose key is being changed) is still used by rows in a child table. Removing it would break those links, so the database refuses unless the foreign key says what to do with the children.
fk_has_children.why_hi: Jo record delete ho raha hai (ya jiski key badal rahi hai) wo abhi child table ki rows mein use ho raha hai. Hatane se wo links toot jaate, isliye database mana karta hai jab tak foreign key na bataye children ka kya karna hai.
fk_has_children.confirm_en: Count the child rows that point to it; after deciding their fate, the delete goes through.
fk_has_children.confirm_hi: Usse judi child rows gino; unka faisla karke delete ho jayega.
fk_has_children.prevent_en: Decide per relation: ON DELETE CASCADE (children go too), SET NULL, or soft-delete (a deleted_at column) for business records.
fk_has_children.prevent_hi: Har relation ke liye tay karo: ON DELETE CASCADE (children bhi jayen), SET NULL, ya business records ke liye soft-delete (deleted_at column).
fk_has_children.short_en: Other rows still point to the record
fk_has_children.short_hi: Doosri rows abhi bhi record ko point karti hain

not_null.title_en: Field "{column}" requires a value but got none
not_null.title_hi: Field "{column}" mein value zaroori hai par khaali bheji gayi
not_null.why_en: The table says "{column}" may never be empty (NOT NULL) and has no default. The statement didn't give it a value (often a new column the app doesn't send yet, or an empty form field turned into NULL).
not_null.why_hi: Table kehti hai "{column}" kabhi khaali nahi ho sakta (NOT NULL) aur iska default nahi. Statement ne value nahi di (aksar naya column jo app abhi nahi bhejti, ya khaali form field NULL ban gaya).
not_null.confirm_en: Saving with a value (or after a default is added) works.
not_null.confirm_hi: Value ke saath (ya default lagne ke baad) save ho jayega.
not_null.prevent_en: Add new NOT NULL columns with a DEFAULT, and validate required fields in the app.
not_null.prevent_hi: Naye NOT NULL columns DEFAULT ke saath jodo, aur zaroori fields app mein check karo.
not_null.short_en: A required field was left empty

value_too_long.title_en: The value is longer than column "{column}" allows
value_too_long.title_hi: Value column "{column}" ki limit se lambi hai
value_too_long.why_en: The column has a maximum length (e.g. VARCHAR(50)). The value is longer, and in strict mode the database refuses rather than silently cutting it.
value_too_long.why_hi: Column ki ek maximum length hoti hai (jaise VARCHAR(50)). Value lambi hai, aur strict mode mein database use chupchaap kaatne ki jagah mana karta hai.
value_too_long.confirm_en: Check the longest value and the column size; after widening, the save works.
value_too_long.confirm_hi: Sabse lambi value aur column size dekho; badhane ke baad save hoga.
value_too_long.prevent_en: Size text columns for real data (names 100+, emails 255, URLs TEXT) and validate length in forms.
value_too_long.prevent_hi: Text columns asli data ke hisaab se rakho (naam 100+, email 255, URL TEXT) aur form mein length check karo.
value_too_long.short_en: Text longer than the column allows
value_too_long.short_hi: Text column ki limit se lamba

out_of_range.title_en: The number is too big for column "{column}"
out_of_range.title_hi: Number column "{column}" ke liye bahut bada hai
out_of_range.why_en: Number columns have limits (TINYINT up to 127, INT about 2.1 billion, DECIMAL(10,2) up to 99,999,999.99). The value is outside that range. A common cause: an INT id running out after years of growth, or money stored with too few digits.
out_of_range.why_hi: Number columns ki limit hoti hai (TINYINT 127 tak, INT lagbhag 2.1 arab, DECIMAL(10,2) 99,999,999.99 tak). Value us range se bahar hai. Aksar: saalon baad INT id khatam, ya paise kam digits mein.
out_of_range.confirm_en: After widening the column type, the save works.
out_of_range.confirm_hi: Column type bada karne ke baad save hoga.
out_of_range.prevent_en: Use BIGINT for ids of growing tables and DECIMAL with enough digits for money from day one.
out_of_range.prevent_hi: Badhti tables ki id ke liye BIGINT aur paise ke liye kaafi digits wala DECIMAL pehle din se rakho.
out_of_range.short_en: A number too big for its column
out_of_range.short_hi: Number column ke liye bahut bada

bad_value_type.title_en: The value "{value}" doesn't fit the column's type
bad_value_type.title_hi: Value "{value}" column ke type mein fit nahi hoti
bad_value_type.why_en: The column expects a number, date or time, but got text it can't read as one (an empty string for a number, '31-02-2026', '1,200' with a comma, or a date in the wrong order).
bad_value_type.why_hi: Column number, date ya time chahta hai, par use aisa text mila jo wo padh nahi sakta (number ki jagah khaali string, '31-02-2026', comma wala '1,200', ya ulta date order).
bad_value_type.confirm_hi: Saaf value ke saath save hoga.
bad_value_type.prevent_en: Convert and validate input in the app (numbers without commas, ISO dates YYYY-MM-DD) and send NULL, not '', for missing numbers.
bad_value_type.prevent_hi: App mein input convert aur check karo (comma bina numbers, ISO date YYYY-MM-DD) aur missing number ke liye '' nahi, NULL bhejo.
bad_value_type.short_en: A value of the wrong type (number/date)

check_violation.title_en: The value breaks a CHECK rule ({constraint})
check_violation.title_hi: Value ek CHECK rule ({constraint}) todti hai
check_violation.why_en: The table has a business rule written as a CHECK (e.g. price > 0, status in a list). The saved value breaks it, so the database refuses.
check_violation.why_hi: Table mein CHECK ke roop mein business rule likha hai (jaise price > 0, status ek list mein). Save ki value use todti hai, isliye database mana karta hai.
check_violation.confirm_en: A value that meets the rule saves fine.
check_violation.confirm_hi: Rule maanne wali value save ho jayegi.
check_violation.prevent_en: Mirror CHECK rules in the app's validation so users see a clear message first.
check_violation.prevent_hi: CHECK rules app ki validation mein bhi rakho taaki user ko pehle saaf message dikhe.
check_violation.short_en: A value that breaks a CHECK rule

charset_mismatch.title_en: The text has characters the column's character set can't store
charset_mismatch.title_hi: Text mein aise characters hain jo column ka charset store nahi kar sakta
charset_mismatch.why_en: Old MySQL 'utf8' stores only 3 bytes per character, so emoji and some Hindi/Asian characters (4 bytes) are refused or turn into ???.
charset_mismatch.why_hi: Purana MySQL 'utf8' ek character ke 3 byte hi rakhta hai, isliye emoji aur kuch Hindi/Asian characters (4 byte) mana ho jaate hain ya ??? ban jaate hain.
charset_mismatch.confirm_en: After converting to utf8mb4, the same text saves and shows correctly.
charset_mismatch.confirm_hi: utf8mb4 mein badalne ke baad wahi text save aur sahi dikhega.
charset_mismatch.prevent_en: Use utf8mb4 everywhere: database, tables, and the app's connection charset.
charset_mismatch.prevent_hi: Har jagah utf8mb4: database, tables aur app ka connection charset.
charset_mismatch.short_en: Characters the column can't store (emoji, some Hindi)
charset_mismatch.short_hi: Aise characters jo column store nahi kar sakta

disk_full.title_hi: Server ki disk bhar gayi hai
disk_full.why_en: The database writes data, logs and temporary sort files to disk. With no space left, writes fail and the database may stop. Usual culprits: binary/WAL logs never cleaned, a huge log or backup file, or temporary files from a big sort.
disk_full.why_hi: Database data, logs aur temporary sort files disk pe likhta hai. Jagah khatam hone par likhna fail hota hai aur database ruk bhi sakta hai. Aksar: binary/WAL logs saaf nahi hue, badi log/backup file, ya bade sort ki temporary files.
disk_full.confirm_en: Free space is back above 15-20% and writes succeed.
disk_full.confirm_hi: Free space 15-20% se upar aa jaye aur likhna chal jaye.
disk_full.prevent_en: Set log retention (binlog_expire_logs_seconds / WAL archiving), move backups off the server, and alert at 80% disk.
disk_full.prevent_hi: Log retention set karo (binlog_expire_logs_seconds / WAL archiving), backups server se bahar rakho, aur 80% disk pe alert lagao.

out_of_memory.title_en: The database ran out of memory
out_of_memory.title_hi: Database ki memory khatam ho gayi
out_of_memory.why_en: When the memory the database is allowed (buffers + per-connection memory x connections) is more than the server has, the operating system kills the database (the OOM killer), or big queries fail. A large unindexed sort/join or too many connections usually tips it over.
out_of_memory.why_hi: Jab database ko di gayi memory (buffers + har connection ki memory x connections) server se zyada ho, to operating system database ko maar deta hai (OOM killer) ya badi queries fail hoti hain. Aksar bina index ka bada sort/join ya bahut connections isko gira dete hain.
out_of_memory.confirm_en: After resizing, memory use stays under about 80% of RAM at peak.
out_of_memory.confirm_hi: Size theek karne ke baad peak pe memory 80% RAM se kam rahegi.
out_of_memory.prevent_en: Size the main buffer to ~50-70% of RAM on a database-only server (less when shared), cap connections with a pool, and index the queries that sort or join big tables.
out_of_memory.prevent_hi: Sirf database wale server pe main buffer RAM ka ~50-70% rakho (shared ho to kam), pool se connections limit karo, aur bade sort/join wali queries pe index lagao.
out_of_memory.short_en: The database ran out of memory

packet_too_large.title_en: A single command or value is bigger than the server accepts
packet_too_large.title_hi: Ek command ya value server ki limit se badi hai
packet_too_large.why_en: The server has a maximum size for one message (max_allowed_packet). A big insert, a large file/image saved in a column, or a huge IN (...) list goes over it, and the server drops the connection.
packet_too_large.why_hi: Server ek message ka maximum size rakhta hai (max_allowed_packet). Bada insert, column mein badi file/image, ya bahut lambi IN (...) list isse upar jaati hai, aur server connection kaat deta hai.
packet_too_large.confirm_en: The same command goes through after the limit is raised or the data is split.
packet_too_large.confirm_hi: Limit badhane ya data todne ke baad wahi command chalegi.
packet_too_large.prevent_en: Store files on disk/object storage and keep only the path; insert in batches of a few hundred rows.
packet_too_large.prevent_hi: Files disk/object storage pe rakho, database mein sirf path; insert sau-do sau rows ke batches mein karo.
packet_too_large.short_en: A command bigger than the server accepts
packet_too_large.short_hi: Server ki limit se badi command

temp_space_full.title_en: A temporary table filled up while running a big query
temp_space_full.title_hi: Badi query ke dauraan temporary table bhar gayi
temp_space_full.why_en: Sorting, grouping or DISTINCT on many rows needs a temporary table. If it grows past its memory/disk limit (or the disk is nearly full), the query fails with 'table is full'.
temp_space_full.why_hi: Bahut rows pe sort, group ya DISTINCT ko temporary table chahiye. Wo apni memory/disk limit se badi ho jaye (ya disk lagbhag bhari ho), to query 'table is full' se fail hoti hai.
temp_space_full.confirm_en: The query finishes after it's indexed or given room.
temp_space_full.confirm_hi: Index ya jagah milne ke baad query poori hogi.
temp_space_full.prevent_en: Index the GROUP BY / ORDER BY columns so no huge temporary table is needed; keep disk headroom.
temp_space_full.prevent_hi: GROUP BY / ORDER BY columns pe index lagao taaki badi temporary table na bane; disk mein jagah rakho.

statement_timeout.title_en: The query was stopped for running too long
statement_timeout.title_hi: Query bahut der chalne ki wajah se rok di gayi
statement_timeout.why_en: A time limit (statement_timeout / max_execution_time) stops queries after a set time. The query is slower than that limit, usually because it scans a whole table without a useful index or waits on a lock.
statement_timeout.why_hi: Ek time limit (statement_timeout / max_execution_time) queries ko tay time ke baad rok deti hai. Query usse dheemi hai, aksar poori table scan karti hai bina index ke, ya kisi lock pe atki hai.
statement_timeout.confirm_en: Run EXPLAIN; after the index the query finishes well inside the limit.
statement_timeout.confirm_hi: EXPLAIN chalao; index ke baad query limit ke andar khatam hogi.
statement_timeout.prevent_en: Keep the timeout (it protects the server), index the filters and joins, and paginate big reads.
statement_timeout.prevent_hi: Timeout rakho (server ko bachata hai), filters/joins pe index lagao, aur bade reads ko pages mein todo.
statement_timeout.short_en: A query stopped for taking too long
statement_timeout.short_hi: Bahut der wali query rok di gayi

full_scan.title_en: The query reads the whole table ({rows} rows) instead of using an index
full_scan.title_hi: Query poori table ({rows} rows) padh rahi hai, index use nahi kar rahi
full_scan.why_en: Without an index on the columns in WHERE / JOIN / ORDER BY, the database has to read every row to find the few you want. Fine at 1,000 rows; very slow at a million.
full_scan.why_hi: WHERE / JOIN / ORDER BY ke columns pe index na ho to database ko kuch rows dhoondhne ke liye har row padhni padti hai. 1,000 rows pe theek; 10 lakh pe bahut dheema.
full_scan.confirm_en: EXPLAIN shows the index used and far fewer rows read.
full_scan.confirm_hi: EXPLAIN mein index dikhega aur bahut kam rows padhi jayengi.
full_scan.prevent_en: Add indexes for the filters your app really uses; review EXPLAIN for new queries; watch the slow query log.
full_scan.prevent_hi: App jo filters sach mein use karti hai unpe index lagao; nayi queries ka EXPLAIN dekho; slow query log pe nazar rakho.
full_scan.short_en: A query reading the whole table (missing index)
full_scan.short_hi: Query poori table padh rahi (index nahi)

deadlock.title_hi: Do transactions ne ek doosre ko rok diya (deadlock)
deadlock.why_en: Transaction A held a row B needed while B held a row A needed. Neither could ever finish, so the database picked one as the victim and rolled it back. It happens when the same rows are updated in different orders by different parts of the app, inside long transactions.
deadlock.why_hi: Transaction A ne wo row pakdi jo B ko chahiye thi, aur B ne wo jo A ko. Dono kabhi poore nahi hote, isliye database ne ek ko victim chun ke rollback kar diya. Ye tab hota hai jab app ke alag hisse same rows alag order mein, lambi transactions mein update karte hain.
deadlock.confirm_en: The deadlock count stops rising after the change.
deadlock.confirm_hi: Badlav ke baad deadlock ki ginti badhna band hogi.
deadlock.prevent_en: Always lock/update rows in the same order (e.g. by id), keep transactions short, index the columns used to find rows to update, and retry a deadlocked transaction automatically (it is safe to retry).
deadlock.prevent_hi: Rows hamesha same order mein lock/update karo (jaise id se), transactions chhoti rakho, update wali rows dhoondhne ke columns pe index lagao, aur deadlock wali transaction automatic retry karo (retry safe hai).
deadlock.short_hi: Do transactions ek doosre ko rok rahi (deadlock)

lock_wait.title_en: The query waited too long for a lock held by another transaction
lock_wait.title_hi: Query ne doosri transaction ke lock ka bahut intezaar kiya
lock_wait.why_en: Another transaction is holding the rows (or table) this one needs and didn't finish in time, often a long-running job, a transaction left open by the app, or a big UPDATE without an index locking many rows.
lock_wait.why_hi: Doosri transaction wo rows (ya table) pakde hue hai jo isko chahiye, aur time pe khatam nahi hui. Aksar lamba chalne wala job, app ki khuli chhodi transaction, ya bina index ka bada UPDATE jo bahut rows lock karta hai.
lock_wait.confirm_en: Find the blocking transaction; after it's fixed, waits disappear.
lock_wait.confirm_hi: Rokne wali transaction dhoondho; theek hone ke baad intezaar khatam.
lock_wait.prevent_en: Keep transactions short, commit promptly, never wait for user input inside a transaction, run big updates in small batches, and index the WHERE of UPDATE/DELETE.
lock_wait.prevent_hi: Transactions chhoti rakho, turant commit karo, transaction ke andar user ka intezaar mat karo, bade updates chhote batches mein, aur UPDATE/DELETE ke WHERE pe index.
lock_wait.short_en: Waiting too long for another transaction's lock
lock_wait.short_hi: Doosri transaction ke lock ka lamba intezaar

serialization_failure.title_en: Two transactions changed the same data at once under strict isolation
serialization_failure.title_hi: Strict isolation mein do transactions ne ek saath same data badla
serialization_failure.why_en: Under SERIALIZABLE (or REPEATABLE READ in PostgreSQL), the database guarantees results as if transactions ran one by one. When two overlap on the same data, one is cancelled so the guarantee holds.
serialization_failure.why_hi: SERIALIZABLE (ya PostgreSQL mein REPEATABLE READ) mein database guarantee deta hai ki result aisa ho jaise transactions ek-ek karke chali. Do transactions same data pe overlap karein to ek cancel hoti hai.
serialization_failure.confirm_en: With the retry in place, the operation succeeds on the next attempt.
serialization_failure.confirm_hi: Retry lagne ke baad agli koshish mein kaam ho jayega.
serialization_failure.prevent_en: Wrap such transactions in an automatic retry (2-3 times with a short wait); use the strict level only where it's needed.
serialization_failure.prevent_hi: Aisi transactions ko automatic retry mein lapeto (2-3 baar, thoda ruk ke); strict level sirf jahan zaroori ho.
serialization_failure.short_en: Two transactions changing the same data at once
serialization_failure.short_hi: Do transactions ek saath same data badal rahi

idle_transaction.title_en: A transaction was left open and is holding locks
idle_transaction.title_hi: Ek transaction khuli chhod di gayi hai aur locks pakde hue hai
idle_transaction.why_en: A connection began a transaction and then went idle without COMMIT or ROLLBACK (an app error path, a debugging session). Everything it touched stays locked and, in PostgreSQL, old row versions can't be cleaned up.
idle_transaction.why_hi: Ek connection ne transaction shuru ki aur bina COMMIT/ROLLBACK ke idle ho gaya (app ka error path, debugging session). Jo bhi usne chhua wo lock rehta hai aur PostgreSQL mein purani rows saaf nahi ho paati.
idle_transaction.confirm_en: After it ends, nothing waits on it any more.
idle_transaction.confirm_hi: Uske khatam hote hi koi uska intezaar nahi karega.
idle_transaction.prevent_en: Always commit/rollback in a finally block; set idle_in_transaction_session_timeout (PostgreSQL) or a short wait_timeout.
idle_transaction.prevent_hi: Commit/rollback hamesha finally block mein; idle_in_transaction_session_timeout (PostgreSQL) ya chhota wait_timeout set karo.
idle_transaction.short_en: A transaction left open, holding locks
idle_transaction.short_hi: Khuli chhodi transaction locks pakde hue

metadata_lock.title_en: A schema change is waiting for (and blocking) the table
metadata_lock.title_hi: Ek schema change table ka intezaar kar raha hai (aur use rok raha hai)
metadata_lock.why_en: ALTER TABLE needs the table to itself. An open transaction that read the table keeps it busy, so the ALTER waits, and every new query on that table queues behind the ALTER: the site freezes.
metadata_lock.why_hi: ALTER TABLE ko table akele chahiye. Table padhne wali ek khuli transaction use busy rakhti hai, ALTER intezaar karta hai, aur us table ki har nayi query ALTER ke peeche line mein lag jaati hai: site atak jaati hai.
metadata_lock.confirm_en: Once the blocker ends, the ALTER finishes and the queue clears.
metadata_lock.confirm_hi: Rokne wala khatam hote hi ALTER poora hoga aur line saaf.
metadata_lock.prevent_en: Run schema changes with a short lock timeout, off-peak, and use online/zero-downtime migration methods for big tables.
metadata_lock.prevent_hi: Schema changes chhote lock timeout ke saath, kam traffic mein chalao, aur badi tables ke liye online/zero-downtime migration tareeke.
metadata_lock.short_en: A schema change stuck waiting for the table
metadata_lock.short_hi: Schema change table ke intezaar mein atka

access_denied.title_hi: Database ne is user/password ko mana kiya
access_denied.why_en: The server checks the user, the password and where the connection comes from. One of them doesn't match: a wrong or changed password, a user that exists only for localhost, or a user name with a different host part.
access_denied.why_hi: Server user, password aur connection kahan se aaya, teeno check karta hai. Inme se ek match nahi: galat ya badla password, user jo sirf localhost ke liye hai, ya alag host wala user naam.
access_denied.confirm_en: Logging in with the corrected user/host works.
access_denied.confirm_hi: Sahi user/host se login ho jayega.
access_denied.prevent_en: Keep credentials in one config (.env), give each app its own user with only the rights it needs, and rotate passwords in all places together.
access_denied.prevent_hi: Credentials ek hi config (.env) mein rakho, har app ka apna user sirf zaroori rights ke saath, aur password badlo to sab jagah ek saath.

host_not_allowed.title_en: The database doesn't accept connections from this machine
host_not_allowed.title_hi: Database is machine se connection accept nahi karta
host_not_allowed.why_en: The user is allowed only from certain hosts (MySQL user@host, PostgreSQL pg_hba.conf). Connections from anywhere else are turned away before the password is even checked.
host_not_allowed.why_hi: User sirf kuch hosts se allowed hai (MySQL user@host, PostgreSQL pg_hba.conf). Baaki jagah se connection password check se pehle hi lauta diya jaata hai.
host_not_allowed.confirm_en: Connecting from the allowed host works.
host_not_allowed.confirm_hi: Allowed host se connect ho jayega.
host_not_allowed.prevent_en: Allow only the app servers' exact IPs, never '%' / 0.0.0.0/0 for admin users.
host_not_allowed.prevent_hi: Sirf app servers ke exact IP allow karo, admin users ke liye kabhi '%' / 0.0.0.0/0 nahi.
host_not_allowed.short_en: This machine isn't allowed to connect
host_not_allowed.short_hi: Is machine ko connect ki ijazat nahi

too_many_connections.title_en: The database reached its maximum number of connections
too_many_connections.title_hi: Database apne maximum connections tak pahunch gaya
too_many_connections.why_en: Each app process opens connections; the server allows only max_connections at once. Traffic spikes, connections never closed (leaks), or slow queries keeping connections busy fill every slot, so new visitors are refused.
too_many_connections.why_hi: Har app process connections kholta hai; server ek saath sirf max_connections allow karta hai. Traffic spike, band na hone wale connections (leak), ya dheemi queries jo connections pakde rehti hain, saare slots bhar dete hain, aur naye visitors mana ho jaate hain.
too_many_connections.confirm_en: At peak, connections in use stay comfortably below the maximum.
too_many_connections.confirm_hi: Peak pe use ho rahe connections maximum se kaafi neeche rahenge.
too_many_connections.prevent_en: Use a connection pool (PgBouncer / ProxySQL / the framework's pool), close connections in a finally block, set a sensible wait_timeout, and fix slow queries that hold connections.
too_many_connections.prevent_hi: Connection pool use karo (PgBouncer / ProxySQL / framework ka pool), connections finally block mein band karo, sahi wait_timeout rakho, aur connections pakadne wali dheemi queries theek karo.

server_unreachable.title_hi: {host}:{port} pe kisi ne jawab nahi diya
server_unreachable.why_en: The connection never reached a database: the database service is stopped or crashed, it listens on another port or only on localhost (bind-address), or a firewall blocks the port.
server_unreachable.why_hi: Connection database tak pahuncha hi nahi: database service band ya crash hai, doosre port pe ya sirf localhost pe sun rahi hai (bind-address), ya firewall port rok raha hai.
server_unreachable.confirm_en: The service is running and the port answers from the app server.
server_unreachable.confirm_hi: Service chal rahi hai aur app server se port jawab deta hai.
server_unreachable.prevent_en: Monitor the service (auto-restart), keep bind-address and firewall rules documented, and alert when the port stops answering.
server_unreachable.prevent_hi: Service monitor karo (auto-restart), bind-address aur firewall rules likh ke rakho, aur port jawab na de to alert.
server_unreachable.short_hi: Database server jawab nahi de raha

connection_lost.title_en: The server closed the connection in the middle
connection_lost.title_hi: Server ne beech mein connection band kar diya
connection_lost.why_en: 'Server has gone away / lost connection' means the connection was alive and then closed: it sat idle longer than wait_timeout, a packet was too large, a query was killed, or the database restarted (often after running out of memory).
connection_lost.why_hi: 'Server has gone away / lost connection' ka matlab connection zinda tha phir band hua: wait_timeout se zyada idle raha, packet bahut bada tha, query kill hui, ya database restart hua (aksar memory khatam hone par).
connection_lost.confirm_en: Long jobs reconnect cleanly and the error stops.
connection_lost.confirm_hi: Lambe jobs saaf reconnect karenge aur error band.
connection_lost.prevent_en: Reconnect or ping before reusing an idle connection (pool 'pre-ping'), keep packets small, and check the error log for restarts.
connection_lost.prevent_hi: Idle connection dobara use karne se pehle reconnect/ping (pool 'pre-ping'), packets chhote rakho, aur restart ke liye error log dekho.
connection_lost.short_en: The connection was cut in the middle

unknown_database.title_en: Database "{db}" doesn't exist on this server
unknown_database.title_hi: Database "{db}" is server pe nahi hai
unknown_database.why_en: The connection asked for a database name the server doesn't have: a typo, a different letter case, or the database was never created/restored on this server.
unknown_database.why_hi: Connection ne aisa database naam maanga jo server pe nahi: spelling, capital/small letters, ya database is server pe bana/restore hi nahi.
unknown_database.confirm_en: Listing the databases shows the exact name; connecting with it works.
unknown_database.confirm_hi: Databases ki list mein sahi naam dikhega; usse connect ho jayega.
unknown_database.prevent_en: Keep the database name in one config value and create it in your setup script.
unknown_database.prevent_hi: Database naam ek config value mein rakho aur setup script mein banao.
unknown_database.short_en: A database name that doesn't exist
unknown_database.short_hi: Aisa database naam jo hai hi nahi

permission_denied.title_en: This user isn't allowed to do that ({token})
permission_denied.title_hi: Is user ko ye ({token}) karne ki ijazat nahi
permission_denied.why_en: Login worked, but the user lacks the right for this action on this table or database (e.g. SELECT, INSERT, CREATE).
permission_denied.why_hi: Login ho gaya, par user ke paas is table/database pe ye kaam (jaise SELECT, INSERT, CREATE) karne ka haq nahi.
permission_denied.confirm_en: The action works after the exact right is granted.
permission_denied.confirm_hi: Sahi haq milne ke baad kaam ho jayega.
permission_denied.prevent_en: Grant only what each app needs (least privilege); separate users for the app, migrations and reporting.
permission_denied.prevent_hi: Har app ko sirf zaroori haq do (least privilege); app, migrations aur reporting ke alag users.
permission_denied.short_en: The user lacks the right for that action
permission_denied.short_hi: User ko us kaam ka haq nahi

ssl_required.title_en: The server requires an encrypted (SSL/TLS) connection
ssl_required.why_en: The server (or this user) only accepts encrypted connections, and the client connected without SSL, or with certificates the server doesn't trust.
ssl_required.why_hi: Server (ya ye user) sirf encrypted connection leta hai, aur client ne bina SSL ke, ya aise certificate se connect kiya jo server nahi maanta.
ssl_required.confirm_hi: SSL ke saath connect ho jayega.
ssl_required.prevent_en: Keep SSL on for remote connections and set it in the app's connection settings, not per script.
ssl_required.prevent_hi: Remote connections ke liye SSL on rakho aur app ki connection settings mein set karo.
ssl_required.short_en: The server requires an encrypted connection

replica_lag.title_en: The replica (copy server) is applying changes later than the primary makes them
replica_lag.title_hi: Replica (copy server) changes primary ke baad der se laga raha hai
replica_lag.why_en: A replica replays every change the primary made, one after another. When the primary writes faster than the replica can replay (one huge UPDATE/DELETE, tables without a primary key under row-based logging, a single replay thread, a weaker or busy replica disk, or long reports on the replica holding replay back), the replica falls behind, so reads sent there show old data.
replica_lag.why_hi: Replica primary ke har change ko ek ke baad ek dobara chalata hai. Jab primary replica se tez likhta hai (ek bahut bada UPDATE/DELETE, row-based logging mein bina primary key ki tables, ek hi replay thread, kamzor ya busy replica disk, ya replica pe lambi reports jo replay rokti hain), to replica peeche reh jata hai aur wahan se padha gaya data purana dikhta hai.
replica_lag.confirm_en: The delay (Seconds_Behind_Source / replay_lag) shrinks to near zero and stays there under normal load.
replica_lag.confirm_hi: Delay (Seconds_Behind_Source / replay_lag) zero ke paas aa jaye aur normal load mein wahin rahe.
replica_lag.prevent_en: Write big changes in small batches, give every table a primary key, enable parallel replay, alert on lag, and send reads that must see the latest data (right after a save) to the primary.
replica_lag.prevent_hi: Bade changes chhote batches mein karo, har table pe primary key rakho, parallel replay on karo, lag pe alert lagao, aur jo read turant naya data dekhna chahiye (save ke turant baad) use primary pe bhejo.
replica_lag.short_en: The replica is behind the primary
replica_lag.short_hi: Replica primary se peeche chal raha hai

replication_stopped.title_en: Replication stopped: the replica hit an error while applying a change
replication_stopped.title_hi: Replication ruk gayi: change lagate waqt replica pe error aaya
replication_stopped.why_en: The replica's data no longer matches the primary's, so a replayed change breaks a rule there: a row the primary inserted already exists on the replica (duplicate key) or a row it updated/deleted is missing (can't find record). It usually starts with someone writing directly on the replica, or an earlier error that was skipped. The replica then stops and stays behind until it's fixed.
replication_stopped.why_hi: Replica ka data primary se match nahi karta, isliye dobara chalaya gaya change wahan rule todta hai: jo row primary ne daali wo replica pe pehle se hai (duplicate key) ya jo row update/delete hui wo replica pe hai hi nahi (can't find record). Aksar shuruaat kisi ke replica pe seedha likhne se hoti hai, ya pehle skip kiye gaye error se. Phir replica ruk jata hai aur theek hone tak peeche rehta hai.
replication_stopped.confirm_en: Replica_SQL_Running / Replica_IO_Running both show Yes (or the subscription worker stays up) and the lag falls back to zero.
replication_stopped.confirm_hi: Replica_SQL_Running / Replica_IO_Running dono Yes dikhayein (ya subscription worker chalta rahe) aur lag wapas zero ho jaye.
replication_stopped.prevent_en: Keep replicas read-only (super_read_only / read_only) so nobody writes there, don't make skipping errors a habit (each skip hides a lost change), and compare primary and replica data from time to time.
replication_stopped.prevent_hi: Replicas read-only rakho (super_read_only / read_only) taaki wahan koi na likhe, errors skip karne ki aadat mat banao (har skip ek khoya hua change chhupata hai), aur primary aur replica ka data beech-beech mein compare karo.
replication_stopped.short_hi: Replication ek error pe ruk gayi

source_log_purged.title_en: The primary deleted the change logs (binary log / WAL) the replica still needed
source_log_purged.title_hi: Primary ne change logs (binary log / WAL) mita diye jo replica ko abhi chahiye the
source_log_purged.why_en: A replica catches up by reading the primary's change log files. The primary removes old files to save disk (a short expiry, a manual purge, or no replication slot / wal_keep_size). If the replica was down or far behind for longer than that, the files it needs are gone and it can't continue: those changes no longer exist on the primary.
source_log_purged.why_hi: Replica primary ki change log files padhkar barabar hota hai. Primary disk bachane ke liye purani files hata deta hai (kam expiry, haath se purge, ya replication slot / wal_keep_size nahi). Agar replica utni der se zyada band ya peeche raha, to zaroori files ja chuki hain aur wo aage nahi badh sakta: wo changes ab primary pe hain hi nahi.
source_log_purged.confirm_en: The rebuilt replica connects, reads from the new position, and its lag drops to zero.
source_log_purged.confirm_hi: Dobara banaya gaya replica connect ho, nayi position se padhe, aur lag zero ho jaye.
source_log_purged.prevent_en: Keep change logs longer than a replica could be down (binlog_expire_logs_seconds / wal_keep_size), check what every replica has read before purging, use replication slots in PostgreSQL with max_slot_wal_keep_size as a disk safety limit, and alert on replica lag early.
source_log_purged.prevent_hi: Change logs utni der rakho jitni der replica band reh sakta hai (binlog_expire_logs_seconds / wal_keep_size), purge se pehle dekho har replica ne kahan tak padha, PostgreSQL mein replication slots aur disk ki hifazat ke liye max_slot_wal_keep_size lagao, aur replica lag pe jaldi alert lagao.
source_log_purged.short_en: The primary already deleted the logs the replica needs
source_log_purged.short_hi: Primary ne wo logs mita diye jo replica ko chahiye

write_on_replica.title_en: The app sent a write to a server that only accepts reads (a replica, or read-only mode is on)
write_on_replica.title_hi: App ne likhne wali query aise server ko bheji jo sirf padhne deta hai (replica, ya read-only mode on hai)
write_on_replica.why_en: Replicas, hot standbys and servers switched to read-only refuse INSERT/UPDATE/DELETE so their data can't drift from the primary. This shows up when the app's connection points at the replica, when a read/write split sends a write to the wrong side, or after a failover when old pooled connections or cached addresses still reach the old primary that is now read-only.
write_on_replica.why_hi: Replicas, hot standbys aur read-only kiye gaye servers INSERT/UPDATE/DELETE mana karte hain taaki unka data primary se alag na ho. Ye tab dikhta hai jab app ka connection replica pe point karta hai, read/write split ek write galat taraf bhej deta hai, ya failover ke baad purane pooled connections ya cached address abhi bhi purane primary tak jaate hain jo ab read-only hai.
write_on_replica.confirm_en: The same write succeeds once it is sent to the primary (read_only = OFF / pg_is_in_recovery() = false there).
write_on_replica.confirm_hi: Wahi write primary pe bhejne par chal jaye (wahan read_only = OFF / pg_is_in_recovery() = false).
write_on_replica.prevent_en: Keep one clear writer address in the app config, let the pool drop connections after a failover, and test writes after every switchover. Don't turn read-only off on a replica to make the error go away: writes there break replication later.
write_on_replica.prevent_hi: App config mein likhne ke liye ek saaf address rakho, failover ke baad pool purane connections chhod de, aur har switchover ke baad write test karo. Error hatane ke liye replica pe read-only band mat karo: wahan ke writes baad mein replication tod dete hain.
write_on_replica.short_hi: Read-only server (replica) pe likhne ki koshish

standby_query_conflict.title_en: A query on the standby was cancelled because it blocked replaying the primary's changes
standby_query_conflict.title_hi: Standby pe query cancel hui kyunki wo primary ke changes ka replay rok rahi thi
standby_query_conflict.why_en: A hot standby must keep replaying the primary's changes. When the primary cleans up old row versions (VACUUM) or takes a strong lock (TRUNCATE, DROP, some ALTERs) that a long query on the standby still needs, the standby waits only max_standby_streaming_delay (30 seconds by default) and then cancels the query so replay can continue.
standby_query_conflict.why_hi: Hot standby ko primary ke changes lagaatar replay karne hote hain. Jab primary purane row versions saaf karta hai (VACUUM) ya strong lock leta hai (TRUNCATE, DROP, kuch ALTER) jo standby ki lambi query ko abhi chahiye, to standby sirf max_standby_streaming_delay (default 30 second) rukta hai aur phir query cancel kar deta hai taaki replay chalta rahe.
standby_query_conflict.confirm_en: The report finishes on the standby, and pg_stat_database_conflicts stops growing.
standby_query_conflict.confirm_hi: Report standby pe poori chale, aur pg_stat_database_conflicts badhna band ho jaye.
standby_query_conflict.prevent_en: Keep standby queries short or retry them; for long reports either turn on hot_standby_feedback (costs some bloat on the primary) or raise max_standby_streaming_delay on a standby used only for reports (costs more lag).
standby_query_conflict.prevent_hi: Standby queries chhoti rakho ya retry karo; lambi reports ke liye ya to hot_standby_feedback on karo (primary pe thoda bloat badhta hai) ya sirf reports wale standby pe max_standby_streaming_delay badhao (lag badhta hai).
standby_query_conflict.short_en: A standby query was cancelled by replay
standby_query_conflict.short_hi: Standby pe query replay ki wajah se cancel hui

wal_retained_by_slot.title_en: A replication slot keeps old WAL files that nobody is reading, so pg_wal keeps growing
wal_retained_by_slot.title_hi: Ek replication slot purani WAL files rakhe hue hai jinhe koi padh nahi raha, isliye pg_wal badhta ja raha hai
wal_retained_by_slot.why_en: A replication slot promises a standby or a logical consumer that the server keeps every WAL file it hasn't read yet. When that standby is gone, broken or far behind, the slot still holds the files, and by default (max_slot_wal_keep_size = -1) there is no limit: pg_wal grows until the disk is full and the server stops.
wal_retained_by_slot.why_hi: Replication slot standby ya logical consumer se vaada karta hai ki jo WAL file usne nahi padhi wo rakhi jayegi. Jab wo standby hata diya gaya, toot gaya ya bahut peeche hai, slot files rakhe rehta hai, aur default (max_slot_wal_keep_size = -1) mein koi limit nahi: pg_wal disk bharne tak badhta hai aur server ruk jata hai.
wal_retained_by_slot.confirm_en: After the unused slot is dropped (or its standby catches up) and a CHECKPOINT runs, pg_wal shrinks.
wal_retained_by_slot.confirm_hi: Bekaar slot drop karne (ya standby ke barabar aane) aur CHECKPOINT ke baad pg_wal chhota ho jaye.
wal_retained_by_slot.prevent_en: Drop slots when you remove a standby or a CDC tool, set max_slot_wal_keep_size as a safety limit, and alert on how much WAL each slot holds.
wal_retained_by_slot.prevent_hi: Standby ya CDC tool hatate waqt uska slot bhi drop karo, max_slot_wal_keep_size ko safety limit ki tarah set karo, aur har slot kitna WAL rok raha hai uspe alert lagao.
wal_retained_by_slot.short_en: A replication slot is holding old WAL
wal_retained_by_slot.short_hi: Replication slot purana WAL rok ke baitha hai

wal_archive_failing.title_en: WAL archiving keeps failing, so PostgreSQL can't remove old WAL files
wal_archive_failing.title_hi: WAL archiving baar baar fail ho rahi hai, isliye PostgreSQL purani WAL files hata nahi pa raha
wal_archive_failing.why_en: With archive_mode on, a WAL file may only be removed after archive_command (or archive_library) has copied it and reported success. If the command fails (full or unmounted backup disk, wrong path, permissions, an expired cloud key), PostgreSQL retries forever and keeps every unarchived file in pg_wal, which keeps growing until the disk fills and the server does a PANIC shutdown.
wal_archive_failing.why_hi: archive_mode on ho to WAL file tabhi hatti hai jab archive_command (ya archive_library) use copy karke success bataye. Command fail ho (backup disk full ya mount nahi, galat path, permission, expired cloud key) to PostgreSQL hamesha retry karta hai aur har bina-archive file pg_wal mein rakhta hai, jo disk bharne tak badhta hai aur server PANIC se band ho jata hai.
wal_archive_failing.confirm_en: pg_stat_archiver shows new archived files after the last failure, and the .ready files in pg_wal/archive_status go away.
wal_archive_failing.confirm_hi: pg_stat_archiver mein aakhri failure ke baad naye archived files dikhein, aur pg_wal/archive_status ki .ready files khatam ho jayein.
wal_archive_failing.prevent_en: Test the archive command by hand after every change, alert on pg_stat_archiver.failed_count and on disk use, and keep the archive destination on a different disk with its own monitoring.
wal_archive_failing.prevent_hi: Har badlaav ke baad archive command haath se test karo, pg_stat_archiver.failed_count aur disk use pe alert lagao, aur archive ki jagah alag disk pe rakho jiski apni monitoring ho.
wal_archive_failing.short_hi: WAL archiving fail ho rahi hai

binlog_not_expiring.title_en: Binary logging is on but old binary log files are never removed automatically
binlog_not_expiring.title_hi: Binary logging on hai lekin purani binary log files apne aap kabhi nahi hat-ti
binlog_not_expiring.why_en: With log_bin on, every change is also written to binary log files. They are only removed when an expiry is set (binlog_expire_logs_seconds / expire_logs_days) or someone runs PURGE BINARY LOGS. MariaDB's built-in default is no expiry; MySQL 8 keeps 30 days, which can still be too much for a busy server on a small disk. The files pile up until the disk is full.
binlog_not_expiring.why_hi: log_bin on ho to har change binary log files mein bhi likha jata hai. Ye tabhi hat-ti hain jab expiry set ho (binlog_expire_logs_seconds / expire_logs_days) ya koi PURGE BINARY LOGS chalaye. MariaDB ka apna default hai: kabhi expire nahi; MySQL 8 30 din rakhta hai, jo chhoti disk wale busy server ke liye bhi zyada ho sakta hai. Files disk bharne tak jama hoti rehti hain.
binlog_not_expiring.confirm_en: SHOW BINARY LOGS lists only recent files and their total size stays steady from day to day.
binlog_not_expiring.confirm_hi: SHOW BINARY LOGS mein sirf haal ki files hon aur unka total size roz same rahe.
binlog_not_expiring.prevent_en: Set binlog_expire_logs_seconds longer than any replica could be behind (and longer than your point-in-time restore window), put it in the config file too, and alert on disk use.
binlog_not_expiring.prevent_hi: binlog_expire_logs_seconds ko replica ke sabse zyada peeche hone ke time (aur point-in-time restore window) se lamba rakho, config file mein bhi likho, aur disk use pe alert lagao.
binlog_not_expiring.short_en: Old binary logs are never removed
binlog_not_expiring.short_hi: Purane binary logs kabhi hat-te nahi

checkpoints_too_frequent.title_en: Checkpoints are happening too often because max_wal_size is too small for the write load
checkpoints_too_frequent.title_hi: Checkpoints bahut jaldi ho rahe hain kyunki write load ke hisaab se max_wal_size chhota hai
checkpoints_too_frequent.why_en: PostgreSQL starts a checkpoint (writing all changed pages to disk) every checkpoint_timeout or when WAL is about to pass max_wal_size. If max_wal_size is small for the amount being written, checkpoints come every few seconds: heavy disk writes, and more WAL, because the first change to each page after a checkpoint writes the whole page into WAL. Writes and queries slow down in waves.
checkpoints_too_frequent.why_hi: PostgreSQL har checkpoint_timeout pe ya jab WAL max_wal_size paar karne wala ho tab checkpoint shuru karta hai (saare badle pages disk pe likhna). Agar likhe ja rahe data ke hisaab se max_wal_size chhota hai, to checkpoint har kuch second mein aata hai: disk pe bhaari writes, aur WAL bhi zyada, kyunki checkpoint ke baad har page ka pehla change poora page WAL mein likhta hai. Writes aur queries lehron mein slow hoti hain.
checkpoints_too_frequent.confirm_en: The 'checkpoints are occurring too frequently' message stops appearing during normal load and most checkpoints are timed, not requested.
checkpoints_too_frequent.confirm_hi: Normal load mein 'checkpoints are occurring too frequently' message aana band ho jaye aur zyada checkpoints timed hon, requested nahi.
checkpoints_too_frequent.prevent_en: Size max_wal_size for your busiest hour (a few GB is common on busy servers), keep checkpoint_timeout at 5-15 minutes, and leave disk headroom: max_wal_size is a soft target, not a hard limit. An occasional warning during a big bulk load is normal.
checkpoints_too_frequent.prevent_hi: max_wal_size apne sabse busy ghante ke hisaab se rakho (busy servers pe kuch GB aam hai), checkpoint_timeout 5-15 minute, aur disk mein jagah chhodo: max_wal_size soft target hai, hard limit nahi. Bade bulk load mein kabhi kabhi warning aana normal hai.
checkpoints_too_frequent.short_hi: Checkpoints bahut jaldi jaldi ho rahe hain

aggregate_misuse.title_en: A total (SUM, COUNT, AVG ...) is used where rows are still being picked
aggregate_misuse.title_hi: Total (SUM, COUNT, AVG ...) us jagah use hua jahan abhi rows chuni ja rahi hain
aggregate_misuse.why_en: WHERE looks at one row at a time, before any group or total exists, so a total can't be tested there. Conditions on totals belong in HAVING, after GROUP BY; in UPDATE/DELETE compare with a subquery that works the total out first.
aggregate_misuse.why_hi: WHERE ek-ek row dekhta hai, group ya total banne se pehle, isliye wahan total check nahi ho sakta. Total wali condition GROUP BY ke baad HAVING mein jaati hai; UPDATE/DELETE mein pehle subquery se total nikaal kar compare karo.
aggregate_misuse.confirm_en: The query runs with the total's condition in HAVING (or against a subquery).
aggregate_misuse.confirm_hi: Total wali condition HAVING (ya subquery) mein rakhne se query chalegi.
aggregate_misuse.prevent_en: Remember the order a query is worked out in: FROM, WHERE (rows), GROUP BY, HAVING (groups), SELECT, ORDER BY.
aggregate_misuse.prevent_hi: Query ka kram yaad rakho: FROM, WHERE (rows), GROUP BY, HAVING (groups), SELECT, ORDER BY.

value_count_mismatch.title_en: The INSERT gives a different number of values than columns
value_count_mismatch.title_hi: INSERT mein columns aur values ki ginti alag hai
value_count_mismatch.why_en: An INSERT pairs values with columns by position: one value for each named column, or, with no column list, one for every column of the table in its order. A missing or extra value (often a new column added to the table, or a comma inside an unquoted value) breaks the pairing, so the database refuses the row.
value_count_mismatch.why_hi: INSERT values ko columns se position ke hisaab se jodta hai: har naam wale column ke liye ek value, ya column list na ho to table ke har column ke liye ek. Ek value kam ya zyada (aksar table mein naya column jud gaya, ya bina quote ki value mein comma) ho to row mana ho jaati hai.
value_count_mismatch.confirm_en: Count the columns and the values: with the same count (and a column list) the INSERT goes in.
value_count_mismatch.confirm_hi: Columns aur values gino: barabar hon (aur column list ho) to INSERT chalega.
value_count_mismatch.prevent_en: Always name the columns in an INSERT (INSERT INTO t (a, b) VALUES (?, ?)), so adding a column to the table later doesn't break it.
value_count_mismatch.prevent_hi: INSERT mein hamesha columns ke naam likho (INSERT INTO t (a, b) VALUES (?, ?)), taaki baad mein naya column judne se ye na toote.
value_count_mismatch.short_en: Columns and values don't match in number
value_count_mismatch.short_hi: Columns aur values ki ginti alag

table_exists.title_hi: {table} naam ki table pehle se hai
table_exists.why_en: CREATE TABLE refuses a name that is already taken in the same database (or schema). It usually means a setup script or migration ran a second time, or two scripts create the same table.
table_exists.why_hi: CREATE TABLE pehle se liya hua naam mana karta hai. Aksar setup script ya migration dobara chal gayi, ya do scripts ek hi table bana rahi hain.
table_exists.confirm_en: List the tables: the name is there already; with IF NOT EXISTS (or a migration that runs once) the script goes through.
table_exists.confirm_hi: Tables ki list dekho: naam pehle se hai; IF NOT EXISTS (ya ek baar chalne wali migration) se script chalegi.
table_exists.prevent_en: Write setup scripts so they can run twice (CREATE TABLE IF NOT EXISTS) and keep one migration per change that runs once.
table_exists.prevent_hi: Setup scripts aise likho ki do baar chal sakein (CREATE TABLE IF NOT EXISTS), aur har badlaav ki ek migration jo ek hi baar chale.
table_exists.short_en: A table with that name already exists
table_exists.short_hi: Us naam ki table pehle se hai

db_file_locked.title_en: The database file is locked by another connection that is writing
db_file_locked.title_hi: Database file ko doosra connection likhte waqt lock kiye hue hai
db_file_locked.why_en: SQLite lets only one connection write to the file at a time. While another connection (another process, thread, or a transaction your own code left open) holds the write lock, a second writer gets 'database is locked' at once unless a busy timeout makes it wait. WAL mode lets readers keep reading meanwhile, but still allows only one writer.
db_file_locked.why_hi: SQLite ek waqt mein sirf ek connection ko file mein likhne deta hai. Jab doosra connection (doosra process, thread, ya aapke code ki khuli chhodi transaction) write lock pakde hai, to doosra writer turant 'database is locked' paata hai, jab tak busy timeout use intezaar na karaye.
db_file_locked.confirm_en: With a busy timeout and short transactions (or WAL mode), the same work finishes without 'database is locked'.
db_file_locked.confirm_hi: Busy timeout aur chhoti transactions (ya WAL mode) ke saath wahi kaam bina 'database is locked' ke poora hota hai.
db_file_locked.prevent_en: Set a busy timeout on every connection, use WAL mode for apps with readers and a writer, keep write transactions short and always commit or roll back (also on errors), and start read-then-write transactions with BEGIN IMMEDIATE. Many writers at once need a client-server database.
db_file_locked.prevent_hi: Har connection pe busy timeout, readers aur writer wale apps ke liye WAL mode, write transactions chhoti aur hamesha commit ya rollback (error pe bhi), aur padh-kar-likhne wali transaction BEGIN IMMEDIATE se shuru karo. Ek saath bahut writers ke liye client-server database chahiye.
db_file_locked.short_en: Another connection holds the database file's write lock
db_file_locked.short_hi: Doosra connection database file ka write lock pakde hai

file_readonly.title_en: The database file can't be written
file_readonly.title_hi: Database file mein likha nahi ja sakta
file_readonly.why_en: SQLite writes to the database file and creates a journal (-journal or -wal) next to it, so the app's user needs write permission on the file AND on its folder. A file copied in by another user (root, a deploy step), a read-only mount, or a connection opened read-only all end in this error.
file_readonly.why_hi: SQLite database file mein likhta hai aur uske paas journal (-journal ya -wal) banata hai, isliye app ke user ko file AUR uske folder dono pe likhne ki permission chahiye. Doosre user (root, deploy step) ki copy ki hui file, read-only mount, ya read-only khula connection, sab yahi error dete hain.
file_readonly.confirm_en: After the app's user owns (or can write) both the file and its folder, the write goes through.
file_readonly.confirm_hi: App ke user ko file aur folder dono pe likhne ki permission milte hi write chalega.
file_readonly.prevent_en: Keep the database in a folder the app's user owns, and don't copy it in as another user.
file_readonly.prevent_hi: Database aise folder mein rakho jo app ke user ka ho, aur use doosre user se copy mat karo.
file_readonly.short_en: The database file (or its folder) isn't writable
file_readonly.short_hi: Database file (ya folder) likhne layak nahi

cannot_open_file.title_en: The database file can't be opened at that path
cannot_open_file.title_hi: Us path pe database file khul nahi rahi
cannot_open_file.why_en: SQLite opens (or creates) a file at the path it is given. A folder in the path that doesn't exist, a relative path read from a different working directory, or no permission on the folder makes the open fail. (A wrong path to a folder that DOES exist silently creates a new, empty database instead, and the next query says 'no such table'.)
cannot_open_file.why_hi: SQLite diye gaye path pe file kholta (ya banata) hai. Path ka koi folder na ho, relative path kisi aur folder se padha jaye, ya folder pe permission na ho to file nahi khulti. (Galat path par folder maujood ho to chupchaap nayi khaali database ban jaati hai, aur agli query 'no such table' kehti hai.)
cannot_open_file.confirm_en: With an absolute path to an existing folder the app can write, the database opens.
cannot_open_file.confirm_hi: Maujood folder ka absolute path (jismein app likh sake) dene se database khulegi.
cannot_open_file.prevent_en: Build the path from the app's own folder (not the current directory), create the folder at setup, and check the file exists before opening it when it must already exist.
cannot_open_file.prevent_hi: Path app ke apne folder se banao (current directory se nahi), setup pe folder banao, aur jo file pehle se honi chahiye uska hona kholne se pehle check karo.
cannot_open_file.short_en: The database file's path can't be opened
cannot_open_file.short_hi: Database file ka path khul nahi raha

file_corrupt.title_en: The file isn't a healthy SQLite database
file_corrupt.title_hi: File sahi SQLite database nahi hai
file_corrupt.why_en: 'database disk image is malformed' means pages inside the file are damaged (a copy taken while the app was writing, a crash on a disk that ignores flushes, deleting the -wal file, or another program writing into it). 'file is not a database' means the path points at some other file, or at an encrypted database opened without its key.
file_corrupt.why_hi: 'database disk image is malformed' ka matlab file ke andar ke pages kharab hain (app likh rahi thi tab copy li, crash, -wal file delete ki, ya kisi aur program ne likha). 'file is not a database' ka matlab path kisi aur file ka hai, ya encrypted database bina key ke khola.
file_corrupt.confirm_en: PRAGMA integrity_check returns ok on the recovered (or correct) file.
file_corrupt.confirm_hi: Theek ki hui (ya sahi) file pe PRAGMA integrity_check 'ok' deta hai.
file_corrupt.prevent_en: Back up with the backup API or VACUUM INTO (never by copying a live file), keep the -wal and -shm files with the database, and let only SQLite write the file.
file_corrupt.prevent_hi: Backup API ya VACUUM INTO se backup lo (chalti file copy karke kabhi nahi), -wal aur -shm files database ke saath rakho, aur file mein sirf SQLite ko likhne do.
file_corrupt.short_en: The database file is damaged or isn't a database
file_corrupt.short_hi: Database file kharab hai ya database hi nahi

alter_not_supported.title_en: SQLite's ALTER TABLE can't make this change
alter_not_supported.title_hi: SQLite ka ALTER TABLE ye badlaav nahi kar sakta
alter_not_supported.why_en: SQLite's ALTER TABLE only renames a table or a column, adds a column, or drops one (from 3.35). Changing a column's type, default or NOT NULL, adding a PRIMARY KEY or UNIQUE column, or adding a NOT NULL column without a default all need the table rebuilt: a new table with the new definition, the rows copied over, the old one dropped and the new one renamed.
alter_not_supported.why_hi: SQLite ka ALTER TABLE sirf table ya column ka naam badalta hai, column jodta hai, ya hata deta hai (3.35 se). Column ka type, default ya NOT NULL badalna, PRIMARY KEY ya UNIQUE column jodna, ya bina default ka NOT NULL column jodna, in sab ke liye table dobara banani padti hai: nayi definition ki table, rows copy, purani drop, nayi ka naam badlo.
alter_not_supported.confirm_en: PRAGMA table_info(table) shows the new definition after the rebuild, and the row count is the same as before.
alter_not_supported.confirm_hi: Rebuild ke baad PRAGMA table_info(table) nayi definition dikhata hai, aur rows ki ginti pehle jitni hai.
alter_not_supported.prevent_en: Do the rebuild inside one transaction with foreign keys switched off, and run PRAGMA foreign_key_check before committing.
alter_not_supported.prevent_hi: Rebuild ek transaction mein, foreign keys band karke karo, aur commit se pehle PRAGMA foreign_key_check chalao.
alter_not_supported.short_en: A table change SQLite's ALTER TABLE can't do
alter_not_supported.short_hi: Table ka badlaav jo SQLite ka ALTER TABLE nahi karta
